partner_context.their_pressure: Ground ride-hail is mature and margin-squeezed across your core markets, and your biggest demand peaks — the Greek islands, the Dalmatian coast, the Riviera, the Gulf — happen exactly where roads run out and the water begins. The next surface of growth isn't another car category; it's the one nobody has claimed.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Bolt already owns the demand in Europe's most water-bound markets. Navier supplies a uniform, software-defined, autonomy-ready foiling fleet that books door-to-door beside a Bolt car at every marina — turning slow ferries and pricey charters into an in-app water tier across the Mediterranean and the Gulf.

hero.title: Bolt × Navier — the European demand platform, now on the water
hero.subtitle: Bolt owns the demand from the Aegean to the Gulf. The coastline is the surface it hasn't claimed yet.
hero.what_we_do_together: We add a Bolt-branded foiling water tier across Bolt's most water-bound markets — the Greek islands, the Dalmatian coast, the Italian Riviera and lagoon, the Côte d'Azur, and the Gulf. Navier supplies the software-defined fleet and the network playbook proven in the Maldives; Bolt brings the demand, the app and the dispatch. Start with one market or commit to the network — the supply standard is identical everywhere.

why_now: Bolt's strongest seasonal demand peaks are in markets where roads run out and the water begins, on ferry fleets that are among Europe's oldest and most polluting — exactly as the EU and Gulf tighten marine emissions and a ~100-vessel Navier network ramps in the Maldives. The in-app water tier is open across the entire Bolt footprint, for now.

network_thesis.headline: One app. Every coastline. The water layer of Bolt — from the Aegean to the Gulf to the Baltic.
network_thesis.body: Bolt operates across 45+ countries; wherever its busiest demand meets the water — the Gulf, the Cyclades, Dalmatia, the Riviera, the Baltic, the Tagus — the road network simply ends. Navier supplies a uniform, software-defined, autonomy-ready foiling fleet that books beside a Bolt car at every marina, identical from Dubai to Athens to Tallinn. Each market below is a parallel entry option — start with the UAE for the cleanest, fully-built marquee proposal (Dubai ↔ Palm ↔ Abu Dhabi), or open any coastline to see the same template applied locally. Pick one market or commit to the network.
network_thesis.how_to_read: Each market is a complete phased proposal. The UAE is the recommended entry point — it is our most fully-fleshed, marquee build (39 grounded corridors, full economics) — but every market stands on its own. Below the sub-proposals sits Bolt's full operating footprint, tiered by how ready each coastline is to render real water geometry.
network_thesis.coverage_note: Bolt operates in 45+ countries The same fleet and in-app tier extend to any harbour Bolt already reaches.

multimodal_fit: Bolt already runs demand, dispatch, pricing and the app. A foiling water tier slots in as a premium mode — the water leg booked door-to-door with a Bolt car at each end, on the same app riders already use.

close.title: From the Aegean to the Gulf, in one app.
close.body: Bolt owns the demand across Europe's and the Gulf's most water-bound markets. Navier supplies the one surface no ride-hail player has claimed. Start with the Greek islands, or commit to the network.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open water and the marinas and piers already in use. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all.
why_navier_now.the_moment: The technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 sold out), decarbonization mandates turned diesel fleets into liabilities, and the hybrid removed the range excuse. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.

objections.concern: Ground ride-hail is our core — why move onto water?
objections.response: Water is the one urban surface Bolt's mission of cheaper, cleaner, car-free mobility hasn't reached. Across the Saronic, the Dalmatian coast and the Gulf, the sea is the fastest line between two points — and no super-app owns it yet.

objections.concern: Is the range enough for the Mediterranean and Gulf?
objections.response: Most coastal and island hops are short — inside the all-electric Pioneer II's 70 nm envelope. The Quanta-LR hybrid covers the longer island and cross-gulf legs up to 700 nm with no charging infrastructure required.

objections.concern: We operate in 45+ countries — how do we launch without huge overhead?
objections.response: You don't build or run the fleet. Navier brings vessels, captains and maintenance; Bolt brings demand, dispatch, the wallet and the brand. Each coastal city is a self-contained pilot on existing berths — no new infrastructure.

objections.concern: Will a water tier fit Bolt's value positioning?
objections.response: Foiling's low energy per passenger-mile is exactly what makes an affordable water option viable. It's cleaner and car-free — on-brand for Bolt — and the resort corridors fund the launch while commuters get a faster crossing.

hero.title: Bolt × Navier — UAE, the anchor market
hero.subtitle: Foil between Dubai's jetties and on to Abu Dhabi, booked in the Bolt app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded electric-foiling tier across Dubai's jetty network, scaling to a Dubai–Abu Dhabi regional corridor — the flagship of the Bolt water network.

markets.why_now: Dubai has the world's densest cluster of luxury hotel and residence jetties, a government actively promoting marine transport, and a clientele that already pays for premium transfers. The Dubai–Abu Dhabi road is a 90-minute-plus drive the water can shortcut. Pioneer II is commercial now and clears every intra-Dubai jetty hop.
markets.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app and wallet: a Bolt car to the jetty, a foiling hop between Palm resorts or across to Abu Dhabi, seamless return — a single premium chain on the corridors where road congestion and heat make driving least attractive.
markets.partner_context: Bolt is expanding its regional premium ambitions. The UAE is where a co-branded marine tier has the highest willingness-to-pay and the strongest government tailwind — the natural anchor to prove the model before replicating it across the network.
markets.why_navier_now: Every intra-Dubai jetty leg (0.5–1.2nm) is trivially inside Pioneer II range. The Dubai Marina–Abu Dhabi Corniche corridor (55.8nm) sits inside the 70nm Pioneer envelope — a genuine near-term regional run, not a roadmap aspiration.
markets.differentiation: Against the chauffeur car: comparable cost, far faster jetty-to-jetty, air-conditioned cabin and a skyline view with zero local emissions. Against the diesel water taxi: foiling-quiet, on-demand and in-app.

markets.why_now: Croatia draws ~20M visitors a year, heavily into the Dalmatian islands reached by slow ferries. Split and Dubrovnik are cruise and tourism hubs choked in summer. Pioneer II is commercial now and every Dalmatian island hop sits inside its range.
markets.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app: a Bolt car to the Split or Dubrovnik waterfront, a foiling hop to the island, a Bolt scooter on arrival — one wallet across the island-hop journey.
markets.partner_context: Bolt is a leading ridehail brand in Croatia. A water tier extends that brand to the islands and the cross-border Kotor leg, on the corridors where ferry slowness and summer crowding frustrate premium riders.
markets.why_navier_now: Every Dalmatian leg (Split–Trogir 8nm, Split–Brač 12nm, Dubrovnik–Kotor 40nm) is inside Pioneer II range — no long-range hull needed for the core network.
markets.differentiation: Against the diesel ferry/excursion boat: faster, on-demand, quiet and all-electric in protected Adriatic waters. Against the coast road: a direct island line that skips the summer jam.

hero.title: Bolt × Navier — Egypt, Red Sea reefs and the Cairo Nile
hero.subtitle: Fly the reef hops and the river commute, in the Bolt app.

markets.why_now: Egypt is targeting 30M tourists, with the Red Sea its fastest-growing coast and a new wave of resort and marina development at El Gouna, Sahl Hasheesh and the Red Sea Riviera. markets.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app, same wallet: a Bolt car to the marina or corniche pier, a foiling Pioneer II across the reef or the river, a Bolt car on arrival.
markets.partner_context: Bolt operates ride-hail at scale across Egyptian cities including Cairo. Egypt is a high-trip, price-sensitive market where the water leg adds a premium tier without new app behaviour.
markets.why_navier_now: Every core Red Sea and Cairo corridor is ≤16nm — squarely Pioneer II, commercial today. The piers exist: El Gouna's lagoon network, Hurghada Marina, Sharm's jetties, and the Cairo corniche. No regional Quanta-LR leg is needed to start.
markets.differentiation: Against the diesel excursion boat: faster to the reefs, no fumes over protected coral, and bookable on demand. Against the Cairo road: a flying river crossing that sidesteps the bridges entirely.

hero.subtitle: Foil across Tallinn Bay and up to Helsinki, booked in Bolt's home-city app.

markets.why_now: Tallinn's waterfront suburbs are growing and the Old City Harbour is a major cruise and ferry node. Pioneer II is commercial now and clears every Tallinn-Bay leg.
markets.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app and wallet in the city where Bolt began: a Bolt car to the Old City Harbour, a foiling hop to Viimsi or across to Helsinki, a Bolt scooter on arrival.
markets.partner_context: Bolt was founded in Tallinn and commands its deepest brand loyalty and operational density here. A flagship water tier in the home market is both a commercial play and a brand statement — the cleanest possible demonstration of Bolt-on-water.
markets.why_navier_now: Every Tallinn-Bay leg (Pirita 4.5nm, Viimsi 5nm) is well inside Pioneer II range, and the Tallinn–Helsinki crossing (43nm) is also within the 70nm envelope — a genuine near-term cross-Gulf corridor, not a roadmap aspiration.
markets.differentiation: Against the suburban road loop: a direct water line that halves the journey with zero local emissions. Against the diesel Gulf ferry: faster and on-demand on the Helsinki run for time-sensitive riders.

markets.summary: Spain is Europe's #1 leisure-boating and second-busiest tourism market, with the densest island-and-coast water demand in the western Med — the Balearics, the Costa Brava and the Costa del Sol — almost none of it monetised in-app. Bolt already runs ride-hail across Spanish cities; the water tier is the missing leg between the airport pier and the island.

hero.title: Bolt × Navier — Spain, the western-Med island shuttle
hero.subtitle: Turn the Balearic and Costa crossings into a flying, in-app water tier.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded foiling water tier across the Balearics, the Costa Brava and the Costa del Sol — booked in the same app as the car, all-electric, no wake, no diesel-ferry timetable.

markets.why_now: Spain hosts ~85M visitors a year and the Balearics alone draw ~16M; the islands are choking on diesel ferries and rental cars while Formentera, Mallorca and Ibiza tighten anchoring and emissions rules. A clean, quiet, on-demand foiling hop is exactly what the regulators and the resorts are asking for — and no super-app has the water leg.
markets.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app, same wallet: a Bolt car to the pier, a foiling Pioneer II across the water, a Bolt scooter on the island. The water leg books door-to-door, captain-partners instead of driver-partners.
markets.partner_context: Bolt is the largest European-owned mobility platform, already operating ride-hail and micromobility across Spain. Spain is a top-five Bolt market by trips and the natural place to prove a Med water tier before extending east.
markets.why_navier_now: Pioneer II is commercial now and clears the short Balearic and Costa hops on a single charge; the Palma–Ibiza–Menorca regional legs (75–130nm) come into reach with Quanta-LR on the 2026+ roadmap. Spain's berths already exist — Palma, Ibiza Town, Formentera (La Savina), Puerto Banús — so we need a pedestal, not a port.
markets.differentiation: Against the diesel fast-ferry: half the door-to-door time, zero wake into protected Posidonia seagrass zones, no fixed timetable, and a fare booked in an app riders already have. Against a private RIB charter: a fraction of the cost and fully electric.

proof_points.claim: The Balearics are a top global leisure-marine market.
proof_points.evidence: Mallorca, Ibiza, Menorca and Formentera draw ~16M visitors a year with intense inter-island and coast-to-island water demand.

proof_points.claim: The corridors are protected and emissions-sensitive.
proof_points.evidence: Formentera caps daily vehicles and the Balearic Posidonia decree restricts anchoring and wake — favouring a quiet, electric, foiling hull.

proof_points.claim: The berths already exist.
proof_points.evidence: Palma, Ibiza Town, La Savina (Formentera), Port de Sóller, Puerto Banús and Marbella are working harbours — Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal.

proof_points.claim: Bolt already owns the rider in Spain.
proof_points.evidence: Bolt operates ride-hail and micromobility across Spanish cities; the water leg slots into an app riders already carry.

objections.concern: The Balearic crossings (Palma–Ibiza) are too long for an 8-pax foiler.
objections.response: Correct — those 75–130nm legs are explicitly Quanta-LR (roadmap), never faked on a Pioneer II. The near-term business is the dense ≤70nm island-and-coast capillary network where Pioneer II is commercial today.

objections.concern: Ferries already run these routes.
objections.response: On fixed timetables, with diesel wake into protected zones, and no door-to-door app booking. The foiling hop wins on time, experience and emissions, and is bookable on demand in the Bolt app.

objections.concern: Seasonality — Spain's water demand is summer-heavy.
objections.response: True, and the model sizes the Prove fleet to the shoulder-season floor; summer is upside. The same hulls redeploy across the Med as the network grows.

markets.the_ask: Co-brand a Spain water tier with Bolt, starting with a 2-boat Prove fleet on the Costa del Sol / Costa Brava capillary hops in 2026 H2, scaling across the Balearic islands as berth agreements land.
markets.close: Spain is the densest leisure-water market in Europe and Bolt already owns the rider. The water tier is the one leg no one has flown — let's fly it.
markets.end_state: A western-Med foiling network — Costa Brava, Costa del Sol and the Balearics — booked in the Bolt app, with Quanta-LR closing the inter-island regional legs.

markets.summary: Stockholm is built on 14 islands across an archipelago of ~30,000 — a city that should move on water but mostly doesn't, beyond a handful of diesel commuter ferries. hero.title: Bolt × Navier — Stockholm, the archipelago water tier
hero.subtitle: Fly the commute across the islands, in the Bolt app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded foiling water tier across central Stockholm and the inner archipelago — all-electric, no wake, booked in the same app as the car.

markets.why_now: Stockholm has ambitious climate-neutral targets, a congested island core, and a strong existing water-commute culture that runs on ageing diesel tonnage. The city is actively electrifying its ferries — an open door for a quiet, fast, zero-emission foiling tier on the dense inner-water legs.
markets.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app, same wallet: a Bolt ride to the quay, a foiling Pioneer II across the water, a Bolt scooter on the far island. The water leg books door-to-door.
markets.partner_context: Bolt is an Estonian company and the dominant European-owned mobility platform across the Nordics and Baltics; Stockholm is a flagship market. A water tier extends Bolt's home-region leadership onto the water it knows best.
markets.why_navier_now: Every core central-Stockholm and inner-archipelago leg is ≤12nm — Pioneer II, commercial now. The quays already exist (Slussen, Nybroplan, Strömkajen, Stadshuskajen). The Åland crossing (75nm) is a Quanta-LR roadmap leg, never faked on a Pioneer II.
markets.differentiation: Against the diesel commuter ferry: faster, quieter, zero-emission, and bookable on demand instead of by timetable. Against the road-and-bridge commute: a direct flying line across water the city is already organised around.

proof_points.claim: Stockholm is a natural water-transport city.
proof_points.evidence: The city spans 14 islands with an established commuter-ferry culture and a 30,000-island archipelago beyond.

proof_points.claim: The city is electrifying its waterborne transport.
proof_points.evidence: Stockholm has active programmes to decarbonise its ferries and meet climate-neutral targets — directly favouring an electric foiler.

proof_points.claim: The quays already exist.
proof_points.evidence: Slussen, Nybroplan, Strömkajen, Stadshuskajen and Djurgården are working passenger quays — Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal.

proof_points.claim: Stockholm is a flagship Bolt market in Bolt's home region.
proof_points.evidence: Bolt operates ride-hail and micromobility across the Nordics/Baltics from its Estonian base.

objections.concern: Stockholm winters ice over.
objections.response: The Prove fleet is sized to the open-water season; the foiling hull's all-electric, all-weather operating envelope is validated on the warmer Med and Gulf legs first, with winter operating limits set conservatively.

objections.concern: The city already runs commuter ferries.

objections.concern: Is there enough premium demand?
objections.response: Central hops compete on time saved against a congested island core, and the archipelago leisure runs (Vaxholm, Drottningholm) carry a clear leisure premium.
